request.query: Finsupp product over support equals product over fintype when g i 0 = 1

items.informal_name: Product over Finite Support Equals Full Product in Finite Type
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_8} {N : Type u_10} [inst : Zero M] [inst_1 : CommMonoid N] [inst_2 : Fintype α]
  (f : α →₀ M) (g : α → M → N), (∀ (i : α), g i 0 = 1) → f.prod g = ∏ i, g i (f i)
items.informal_description: For a finite type $\alpha$, a finite support function $f : \alpha \to_0 M$, and a function $g : \alpha \to M \to N$ where $g(i)(0) = 1$ for all $i \in \alpha$ (with $N$ a commutative monoid), the product of $g$ over the support of $f$ equals the product of $g(i)(f(i))$ over all elements $i \in \alpha$. Formally, $\prod_{a \in \text{support}(f)} g(a, f(a)) = \prod_{i \in \alpha} g(i, f(i))$.

items.informal_name: Product of onFinset Function Equals Product over Finite Set
items.informal_description: Let $ s $ be a finite set in $ \alpha $, $ f : \alpha \to M $, and $ g : \alpha \to M \to N $ where $ N $ is a commutative monoid. If $ f(a) \neq 0 $ implies $ a \in s $ and $ g(a, 0) = 1 $ for all $ a $, then the product of $ g(a, f(a)) $ over the support of the finite support function $ \text{onFinset}(s, f) $ equals the product of $ g(a, f(a)) $ for all $ a \in s $.

items.informal_name: Product Equality for Dependent Finite Support Functions on Finite Types
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u} {γ : Type w} {β : ι → Type v} [inst : DecidableEq ι] [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : (i : ι) → Zero (β i)]
  [inst_3 : (i : ι) → (x : β i) → Decidable (x ≠ 0)] [inst_4 : CommMonoid γ] (v : Π₀ (i : ι), β i)
  {f : (i : ι) → β i → γ}, (∀ (i : ι), f i 0 = 1) → v.prod f = ∏ i, f i (DFinsupp.equivFunOnFintype v i)
items.informal_description: For a finite index type $\iota$ and a commutative monoid $\gamma$, given a dependent finite support function $v : \Pi₀ (i : \iota), \beta(i)$ and a function $f : \forall i, \beta(i) \to \gamma$ satisfying $f(i)(0) = 1$ for all $i$, the product of $v$ with respect to $f$ equals the product over all $i : \iota$ of $f(i)(v_i)$. This equality holds because the canonical equivalence between dependent finite support functions and all functions on finite types reduces the product over the support to a product over the entire finite index set.

items.informal_name: Product over Superset with Identity Padding Equals Support Product
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_8} {N : Type u_10} [inst : Zero M] [inst_1 : CommMonoid N] (f : α →₀ M) {s : Finset α},
  f.support ⊆ s → ∀ (g : α → M → N), (∀ i ∈ s, g i 0 = 1) → f.prod g = ∏ x ∈ s, g x (f x)
items.informal_description: Let $ f : \alpha \to_0 M $ be a finite support function with values in a monoid $ M $, let $ s $ be a finite set such that the support of $ f $ is contained in $ s $, and let $ g : \alpha \times M \to N $ be a function into a commutative monoid $ N $ satisfying $ g(i, 0) = 1 $ for all $ i \in s $. Then, the product of $ g(a, f(a)) $ over all $ a $ in the support of $ f $ equals the product of $ g(x, f(x)) $ over all $ x $ in $ s $.

items.informal_name: Finite Product Over Multiplicative Support Equals Total Product
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_5} [inst : CommMonoid M] (f : α → M),
  ∏ᶠ (a : α) (_ : a ∈ Function.mulSupport f), f a = ∏ᶠ (a : α), f a
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \alpha \to M $ where $ M $ is a commutative monoid, the finite product of $ f(a) $ over the multiplicative support of $ f $ is equal to the finite product of $ f(a) $ over all elements of $ \alpha $.
